**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Computer Science 2 (0795), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer any SIX questions. All questions carry 17 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An object-oriented program is being written to store details of and play media files that are stored on a computer. A class **MediaFile** has been created and two subclasses, **VideoFile** and **MusicFile** are to be developed. The classes VideoFile and MusicFile are types of MediaFile. In object-oriented programing,

(a) Give a diagrammatic representation of these classes. State and justify the object-oriented concept that best relates the classes. (3 marks)

(b) Give in pseudocode, a method (loosely, a procedure or function) to print the artist of a **Music_file** and another method by the same name to print the title of a **Video_file**. What main object-oriented programming language concept permits one to call this method with any media file object and correctly print the right values? Justify your answer. (4 marks)

(c) Briefly explain how one would exploit encapsulation in order to make sure methods in **MusicFile** object do not access or modify those in **VideoFile**. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Class diagram and concept (3 marks)**

```text
              +------------------+
              |    MediaFile     |
              |------------------|
              | title            |
              | fileSize         |
              | play()           |
              | printDetails()   |
              +------------------+
                  ^          ^
                  |          |     (arrows with open heads = "is a")
     +------------------+  +------------------+
     |    VideoFile     |  |    MusicFile     |
     |------------------|  |------------------|
     | resolution       |  | artist           |
     | printDetails()   |  | printDetails()   |
     +------------------+  +------------------+
```

The concept that relates the classes is **inheritance**. VideoFile and MusicFile are specialised kinds of MediaFile (an "is-a" relationship: a video file *is a* media file), so they inherit the attributes and methods common to all media files (title, file size, play) from the superclass MediaFile and add or redefine only what is specific to them. This justifies the choice: it avoids duplicating code and expresses that both subclasses are types of MediaFile.

**(b) Methods and polymorphism (4 marks)**

```text
CLASS MediaFile
    PROCEDURE printDetails()          ; general version, overridden below
        OUTPUT "Media file: ", self.title
    END PROCEDURE
END CLASS

CLASS MusicFile INHERITS MediaFile
    PROCEDURE printDetails()          ; prints the artist
        OUTPUT "Artist: ", self.artist
    END PROCEDURE
END CLASS

CLASS VideoFile INHERITS MediaFile
    PROCEDURE printDetails()          ; prints the title
        OUTPUT "Title: ", self.title
    END PROCEDURE
END CLASS
```

Calling the method with any media file object:

```text
FOR EACH m IN mediaList               ; m may be a MusicFile or a VideoFile
    m.printDetails()
NEXT m
```

The concept is **polymorphism** (here method overriding with dynamic or late binding). The same method name `printDetails` is defined in several classes, and at run time the version belonging to the real class of the object is the one executed: a MusicFile object prints its artist and a VideoFile object prints its title, although the calling code does not need to know which kind of file it holds.

**(c) Encapsulation (3 marks)**

Encapsulation means bundling the data (attributes) of a class with the methods that work on it and hiding the data from the outside. To make sure the methods of MusicFile cannot access or modify those of VideoFile (and vice versa):

- declare the attributes of each class as **private** (for example `artist` in MusicFile and `resolution` and `title` in VideoFile), so that only the methods of the class that owns them can read or change them directly;
- give each class a **public interface** (methods such as `getArtist()`, `setArtist()`, `printDetails()`), the only way for outside code to use the object; a MusicFile method can reach a VideoFile object only through the public methods that VideoFile chooses to expose, and the internal implementation can change without affecting the other class;
- keep the own attributes of each subclass private (never public), and let the shared data of MediaFile be reached only through its public get and set methods, so that MusicFile and VideoFile stay independent of each other.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) For children, a tourist attraction has a daily charge of 5000 FCFA on weekdays and 7500 FCFA on weekends or bank holidays. Adults are charged 8000 FCFA on weekdays and 12000 FCFA on weekends and bank holidays. Write a pseudocode algorithm that allows the user to calculate the charge for a visitor. (4 marks)

(b) Explain in words how you could modify your program in (ii)a so that it recursively calls itself but also checks that the recursion terminates. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Pseudocode (4 marks)**

The user enters the type of visitor and the type of day; selection (IF) chooses the charge, which is then displayed.

```text
OUTPUT "Visitor type (C = child, A = adult): "
INPUT visitor
OUTPUT "Day (W = weekday, E = weekend or bank holiday): "
INPUT day

IF visitor = "C" THEN
    IF day = "W" THEN
        charge <- 5000
    ELSE
        charge <- 7500
    END IF
ELSE
    IF day = "W" THEN
        charge <- 8000
    ELSE
        charge <- 12000
    END IF
END IF

OUTPUT "The charge is ", charge, " FCFA"
```

**Check by simulation.** A Python translation of this algorithm gives the four possible charges: child on a weekday 5000, child at a weekend or bank holiday 7500, adult on a weekday 8000, adult at a weekend or bank holiday 12000 FCFA.

**(b) Recursive version (3 marks)**

Turn the calculation into a procedure `TotalCharge(n)` that works out the charge for a group of $n$ visitors:

- **Recursive case:** if $n > 0$, read the type of visitor and the day for one visitor, compute that visitor's charge with the same selection structure as in (a), then **call itself** with one visitor fewer, `TotalCharge(n - 1)`, and add the value returned to the visitor's charge.
- **Base case (termination):** if $n = 0$, there is nobody left, so the procedure stops calling itself and returns 0.
- **Guaranteeing termination:** every call receives a smaller value ($n - 1$), moving the problem towards the base case; the procedure must also check at the start that $n$ is a whole number and not negative (if $n < 0$ it returns 0 or reports an error), otherwise the value would never reach 0 and the recursion would not stop.

For example, for a child on a weekday, an adult at a weekend and an adult on a weekday, `TotalCharge(3)` returns $5000 + 12000 + 8000 = 25000$ FCFA (checked with a Python version of the recursion). A similar approach is to call the procedure again when the input is invalid, allowing only a limited number of attempts so that the recursion also terminates.
